text:
simon: Heads up — us-west-2 is showing sustained GPU node reboots and pod churn. We're seeing degraded capacity and tail latency spikes. Planning a graceful GSLB weight drain to eu-west-1 + ap-south-1 in a staged rollout starting in ~5m.

aj: Is this cloud maintenance or capacity eviction? any ETA on nodes coming back?

simon: Root cause looks like a combination of host maintenance + kernel OOMs on a couple hosts (investigating). Nodes are rebooting intermittently. No confirmed maintenance window from provider yet.

aj: OK. For the GSLB shift, prefer gradual weights to avoid request thrash. Can you paste the commands you'll run?

simon: Will do. Plan: 1) lower us-west-2 weight to 20% 2) increase eu/ap to absorb 80% with a canary route 3) bump health-check thresholds to avoid transient flaps 4) monitor request traces and token-level errors.

simon: Commands: ```
# set initial staged weights
rwctl routing set-weight --region us-west-2 --weight 0.2 --policy gslb
rwctl routing set-weight --region eu-west-1 --weight 0.5 --policy gslb
rwctl routing set-weight --region ap-south-1 --weight 0.3 --policy gslb
# optional: create a canary prefix to verify model latency
rwctl routing create-canary --prefix /canary/gpu --regions eu-west-1,ap-south-1 --weight 0.1
```

maria: Also recommend increasing the health-check failure threshold from 3 -> 5 and DNS TTL to 30s for this operation so small flaps don't force rebalances.

ryan: What's the expected cost delta if we hold additional capacity in eu-west? Need to flag finance if burn rises.

simon: Short term spike maybe ~8-12% extra because of overprovisioning and cross-region egress. We'll keep the canary small and rollback quickly if cost or errors spike.

ops-bot: [ALERT] GSLB health probe failures detected for region us-west-2 (probe-failures=18, last=2m). URL: https://status.internal/gslb/us-west-2

aj: I'm going to run the first weight change now. I'll do it in 3 steps over 10 minutes. Calling it out here so oncall doesn't double-shift.

aj: Step 1 -> setting us-west-2 -> 0.5, eu-west-1 -> 0.3, ap-south-1 -> 0.2 (small move)

simon: Ack. Watching traces and queue depths.

aj: Step 2 -> setting us-west-2 -> 0.2, eu-west-1 -> 0.5, ap-south-1 -> 0.3

maria: Noted increased 5xx on one route (model-x) from eu-west-1 canary. Rolling the canary back to 0.02 while we inspect.

aj: rolled canary down. Adjusting weights to compensate: eu-west-1 -> 0.45, ap-south-1 -> 0.35

ryan: From ops dashboards looks like latency normalized for most routes. Any customer hits?

simon: No customer-facing errors besides increased retries in telemetry for ~4 customers — reaching out to their SEs proactively.

maria: Filed a quick ticket to node team: "Investigate kernel OOM pattern on hosts i-0a1b2c" with logs attached. Ticket #INFRA-4821

ops-bot: [INFO] Route weights updated by aj: us-west-2=0.2, eu-west-1=0.45, ap-south-1=0.35

aj: Leaving weights here for now. Will monitor for 30m, then either move back or continue draining depending on node recoveries.

simon: Thanks. Follow-up actions: 1) infra team to repro kernel OOMs and roll OS patch 2) consider short-term reserved instances for us-west-2 if provider instability persists 3) update runbook with graceful GSLB drain steps (TTL/HC knobs).

ryan: I'll ping finance if we need temporary reserved capacity.

maria: Adding runbook note about canary rollback thresholds and cost escalation matrix.

aj: closing the loop here — will post final status after 30m. :thumbsup:

simon: Good job — keeping this gradual avoided mass evictions.

aj: final status: nodes in us-west-2 still flaky, keeping weights until patch. Last check: 30m stable on eu/ap routes, customer impact minimal.

ops-bot: [RESOLVED] Incident category: capacity-degradation (incident_id=INC-2026-03). Follow-ups: INFRA-4821, RUNBOOK-79.
